title_zh: 不许进儿童池（No Kiddie Pool）：Situational Awareness 被强平、Exoma 登记日乌龙与 SpaceX 结构性票据
subtitle_zh: AI 对冲基金 Situational Awareness 因短期融资被强平、Exoma 登记日乌龙，以及银行借结构性票据向散户买入 SpaceX 看跌期权。
summary_zh: 本期由 Matt Levine 主持，Sylvia Killingsworth 首次担任客座主持。话题一是对冲基金 Situational Awareness：由前 OpenAI 员工 Leopold Aschenbrenner 创立，凭押注 AI 做大两年间回报约一千个百分点，但近几周 AI 回撤，加上他做多 AI 与存储芯片、做空软件公司两头不利，主经纪商发出追加保证金通知，被迫强平大量仓位，Citadel 折价接手其股票头寸，管理规模降到约一百亿美元。Matt 借此指出：用短期融资支撑长期高波动押注必然脆弱，回报过高本身就是杠杆的危险信号。话题二是生物科技公司 Exoma：以每股三十九美元现金加一份或有价值权（CVR）卖给 Ligand，却把登记日定在合并完成前一天，引发对登记日与 T+1 结算的混乱解读，随后撤回、按完成时点处理，Matt 认为这是把 CVR 误当成需要登记日的股息式分派。话题三是 SpaceX 结构性票据：表面是散户买入带下行保护的产品，实质是银行借此向散户买入 SpaceX 深度虚值看跌期权，因为这类保险很难直接从市场获得。

turns.en: So there's a Bloomberg story this week about basically banks or financial firms are rolling out structured notes on SpaceX. So SpaceX went public about a month ago. Its stock has fallen below the IP price. It went up and then it went down. It's not a rough time, and banks are rushing to sell people structured notes on SpaceX. And I think the stuff like this is interesting because a structured note is kind of There's two ways to think about the trade, right. One way is we have these let's say retail clients, high net worth clients, individual clients, and we want to sell them stuff that they want to buy. And so the story here is something like SpaceX went down. We want to give you something that has SpaceX in the name, but like protects you from some downside won't go down as much as SpaceX. And so the Bloomberg story by lu Wang was like about banks are rushing to sell these high net worth clients something that looks like SpaceX with some downside protection. But if you look at the notes like they are something slightly different, which is the other way to think about structured notes, is that banks have these retail clients. The retail clients, yeah, the kind of buy whatever you sell them, and so the job of the structured notes business is to sell them the stuff you want to sell. And what happened here, I think it looks to me from looking at these structured debts is that the banks wanted to buy puts on SpaceX. They wanted to buy protection against SpaceX going down, probably because they had other clients who wanted to buy it from them, and they wanted to know buy it from someone else. And it is actually very easy to buy puts in the form of a structured note, and so the structured nottes have like roughly the shape of the retail investors give the bank money, The bank holds onto the money for a while for a year or two. When the note expires in a year or two, the bank gives the customers money back with a big interest payment. So like there's one, there's a Morgan Stanley one that pays back one hundred and forty cents on the dollars. So you put a one hundred dollars today and eighteen months you give back one hundred and forty dollars unless SpaceX is down a lot. I think in that case it's down fifty percent. SpaceX is down fifty percent, then you lose the same percentage of your money. So if you put a one hundred dollars SpaceX is down sixty percent, you get back forty dollars. So that to Morgan Stanley looks like they have bought a put on SpaceX. Yeah, like they have bought insurance on SpaceX's stock from their retail customers. It doesn't say that, right. What it says is like, this is a thing.
turns.zh: 这周 Bloomberg 有一篇报道，大意是银行或金融公司正在推出以 SpaceX 为标的的结构性票据。SpaceX 大约一个月前上市，股价已经跌破发行价——先涨后跌，日子不太好过，而银行正争相向人们推销 SpaceX 的结构性票据。我觉得这类东西有意思，是因为结构性票据这个交易有两种理解方式。一种是：我们有一批零售客户、高净值客户、个人客户，我们想卖给他们想买的东西。所以这里的说法大致是『SpaceX 跌了，我们想给你一个名字里带 SpaceX、但能保护你一部分下行、不会像 SpaceX 那样跌那么多的产品』。Lu Wang 那篇 Bloomberg 报道讲的就是银行争相向这些高净值客户推销一种看起来像 SpaceX、又带下行保护的东西。但如果你去看这些票据本身，它们其实是稍微不同的东西——这就是理解结构性票据的另一种方式：银行有这些零售客户，这些客户基本上你卖什么他们就买什么，所以结构性票据业务的任务就是把你想卖的东西卖给他们。而这里发生的事，我看这些结构性债务后的判断是：银行想买 SpaceX 的看跌期权（put），想买 SpaceX 下跌时的保护，很可能是因为他们有别的客户想从他们手里买这个，而他们又想从别人那里买进。而以结构性票据的形式买看跌期权其实非常容易，所以这些票据大致的形状是：零售投资者把钱给银行，银行把钱持有一段时间，一年或两年；票据到期时，银行把钱还给客户并附一大笔利息。比如有一支 Morgan Stanley 的产品按每美元偿还一百四十美分，也就是你今天投入一百美元，十八个月后还你一百四十美元——除非 SpaceX 跌得很惨。我记得在那种情况下是跌百分之五十，如果 SpaceX 跌了百分之五十，你就按同样比例亏钱。所以如果你投一百美元、SpaceX 跌了百分之六十，你只拿回四十美元。对 Morgan Stanley 来说，这看起来就像他们买了 SpaceX 的看跌期权——他们从零售客户那里买到了 SpaceX 股票的保险。它不会这么写，它写的是『这是一个……』

turns.en: Marketing is sort of like you're getting some sort of SpaceX pad that is like downside protected or whatever. But from Morgan Stanley's perspective, they're sourcing puts on SpaceX and it's hard to buy very out of the money puts. Why two reasons, So that's what you're warning something. You just want to buy insurance against SpaceX going down a lot, right, So you're like, I don't care if if it goes down ten percent, that's fine, but like, I want to buy insurance against it going down fifty percent. One. People don't like to sell you that because that's very out of the money put it's not worth very much. It has a very low probability of paying out, and so they can't charge you that much for it because it's like improbable, but in the state of the world where it pays out, it's very bad for them. They have to pad a lot of money. And also like something has gone wrong like the AI bad. Yeah, like the AI boom has collapsed or something. So in a world where SpaceX insurance pays out, like the people selling it to you will be very sad, and so they don't want to sell you that except at a very high price. And the other reason is like conversely, you don't want to buy that insurance from like some hedge fund. Yeah, because in a world where that insurance pays out like that hedge fund might have.
turns.zh: 营销话术大致是『你买到的是某种带下行保护的 SpaceX 产品』之类的。但从 Morgan Stanley 的角度看，他们是在获取 SpaceX 的看跌期权，而深度虚值（out of the money）的看跌期权很难买到，有两个原因。你想买的其实是——你只想买 SpaceX 大幅下跌时的保险，对吧，所以你会说『跌百分之十我不在乎，那没事，但我想买它跌百分之五十时的保险』。第一，别人不太愿意卖给你，因为那是很深度虚值的看跌期权，本身不值多少钱，赔付概率很低，所以他们没法向你收很多钱（因为不太可能发生），可一旦在真的赔付的那个世界里，对他们非常不利，他们要赔很多钱；而且往往意味着出了大问题，比如 AI——AI 繁荣崩了之类。所以在 SpaceX 保险会赔付的那个世界里，卖保险给你的人会非常惨，因此除非价格很高，他们不想卖给你。第二个原因正相反：你也不想从某个对冲基金那里买这种保险，因为在那个保险会赔付的世界里，那家对冲基金可能已经——

turns.en: Blown up, right, right, So you're saying, this is a way for them to get out that put without touching the very out of the money actual put.
turns.zh: ……爆掉了。对，对。所以你是说，这是他们拿到那个看跌期权的一种方式，而不必去碰那个真正深度虚值的看跌期权本身。

turns.en: This is a way for them to buy very out of the money puts on SpaceX from people who don't quite realize that they're selling out of the money puts on SpaceX their retail customers.
turns.zh: 这就是他们从那些没太意识到自己正在卖出 SpaceX 深度虚值看跌期权的人——也就是他们的零售客户——那里买入 SpaceX 深度虚值看跌期权的方式。

turns.en: So they didn't want to do it, so they got their retail customers.
turns.zh: 所以他们不想直接做，就让自己的零售客户来做。

turns.en: Of course. Of course, that's what structured nottes are. It's like structured notes are sourcing like weird volatility risk from your retail customers so that you can sell it to hedgepes.
turns.zh: 当然，当然，结构性票据就是这么回事。结构性票据就是从你的零售客户那里获取各种古怪的波动率风险，好让你能把它卖给对冲基金。

turns.en: So that's not a structured note. Was just a note with like a derivative in it.
turns.zh: 所以那不算真正的结构性票据，只是一支里面嵌了衍生品的票据。

turns.en: Yeah, but like why did they put that derivave? And I mean part of it is marketing. Part of it is like people want particular trades right like it. But part of it is like they have some inventory and they're like what weird stuff can we.
turns.zh: 对，但他们为什么要放那个衍生品进去？我的意思是，一部分是营销，一部分是人们想要特定的交易……但还有一部分是他们手里有些『库存』，就想『我们能拼出什么古怪的东西来』。

turns.en: You're sort of meeting several obligations.
turns.zh: 你其实是在同时满足好几项需求。

turns.en: At once, right, and like they're real magic thinking.
turns.zh: 同时满足，对。而且这里真有点『魔法思维』。

turns.en: About structured notes differently now, Yeah, you tell me.
turns.zh: 我现在对结构性票据的看法不一样了。是啊，是你告诉我的。

turns.en: That you keep getting pitched structured notes.
turns.zh: 就是你会不断被人推销结构性票据。

turns.en: Should I should? I guess I should be more skeptical.
turns.zh: 我该……我想我应该更怀疑一些。

turns.en: I think I told my financial advisor on my first day, like, by the way, I'm a former derivative structure, so don't come out with these structure does But no, Like I mean, like the whole game is like you're in the derivative lab. You're like a bucket of stuff, and you like pick stuff out of the bucket of stuff and you're like, how do I make this thing look cool? Like how do I make this How do I tell a story that's like, oh, this stuff is you should really buy this stuffy?
turns.zh: 我想我第一天就跟我的理财顾问说了：『顺便，我是前衍生品结构化人员，所以别拿这些结构性票据来忽悠我。』不过——我是说，整件事的玩法就是：你在衍生品实验室里，面前有一桶各种零件，你从桶里挑出东西，然后想『我怎么把这东西做得看起来很酷？我怎么讲一个故事，让人『哦，这东西你真该买』？』

turns.en: As you said, you have inventory.
turns.zh: 就像你说的，你有『库存』。

turns.en: It's like, yeah, it's interesting because you don't exactly have inventory. You have like some list of like options, exposures and like volatilities, and you're like, how can I turn this into a product that people will be excited to buy and their answers and like a lot of what banks are doing is you know, buying some puts from retail. But like you never say that.
turns.zh: 是这样，有意思的是你并不真的有『库存』，你有的更像是一张清单：各种期权敞口、波动率之类，然后你想『我怎么把这些变成一个大家会兴奋想买的产品』，答案往往是——银行做的很多事情其实就是『从零售客户那里买一些看跌期权』，但你永远不会这么直说。

turns.en: Is this financialization? Is this financializing something?
turns.zh: 这算金融化（financialization）吗？这是在把什么东西金融化吗？

turns.en: Is it financializing SpaceX stuff? M I mean this is just like it's just like you know, this is the business structure. Notes are old and noble business. And that was the Money Stuff Podcast.
turns.zh: 是把 SpaceX 的东西金融化吗？嗯，我是说，这就是……结构性票据是一门古老而体面的生意。以上就是本期 Money Stuff 播客。
